key_insight: AI racks carry as much host DRAM as HBM (DGX H200: 2 TB vs 1.1 TB; GB300 NVL72: ~17 vs ~21 TB). Deleting its jobs is a big lever.
killer_doubt: Host DRAM is becoming the KV tier and coherent capacity (Vera: 1.5 TB per CPU). Async checkpoint staging needs ~16 B/param, so the real cut may be 2x, not 8x.
decisive_experiment: On rented 8-GPU nodes, cap host memory with cgroups at 256 GB vs 2 TB. Run training (GDS + nvCOMP data path, GPU-to-NVMe checkpoints) and inference (NVMe KV tier). Compare throughput and TTFT. About $100-150k.
prior_art: NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage, nvCOMP/DALI GPU decode, DeepSpeed ZeRO-Infinity/FastPersist NVMe paths. No one has published a host-DRAM-minimal AI node specification.

key_insight: Human think time (5-60 s) exceeds NVMe restore (~1-2 s for a 10 GB, 32k-token 70B KV), so flash can replace the DRAM/CXL KV tier with no visible TTFT cost.
killer_doubt: Aggregate flash bandwidth: 200 sessions per node, each turning every ~40 s at 10 GB, need ~50 GB/s, about half of eight Gen5 drives. False-positive prefetches multiply that.
decisive_experiment: vLLM+LMCache with an NVMe-only KV tier (no DRAM tier). Replay multi-turn chat traces plus a 50-user typing-signal study. Measure TTFT, prefetch hit and false-positive rates, and DRAM saved against a Mooncake-style DRAM tier. About $80k.
prior_art: CachedAttention (2024) prefetches from disk at queue entry; LMCache, Mooncake and Cake tier KV to disk. Typing-signal trigger: none found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Duplicate of I-08555, which states the same typing-indicator KV prefetch more concretely. Merge it there. Its add-on, keeping parked KV compressed, stacks with I-04883.
killer_doubt: Same as I-08555: ~50 GB/s of aggregate flash restore bandwidth per 200-session node, plus wasted prefetches when a tab gains focus but no message follows.
decisive_experiment: Covered by the I-08555 experiment. Add a compressed-at-rest arm (FP8/INT4 KV on flash) to measure how restore bandwidth falls against accuracy.
prior_art: CachedAttention, LMCache, Mooncake (KV offload to SSD); in-batch duplicate I-08555.

key_insight: An idle agent holds GPU KV and CPU sandbox DRAM, each idle while the other works. Co-hibernate both under one budget, waking on the LLM's tool-call tokens.
killer_doubt: A 32 GB GQA-70B KV restore at ~10 GB/s takes ~3 s, longer than a typical tool call. KV hibernation pays only on human waits: likely 2-4x, not 10-20x.
decisive_experiment: Run OpenHands/SWE-agent traces on vLLM+LMCache with Firecracker sandboxes. Measure the idle-gap distribution, resident GB per concurrent agent and added latency under joint hibernation. About $100k.
prior_art: InferCept (ICML 2024) handles KV during tool calls; E2B/Firecracker snapshot-restore; TVCache (ICML 2026) snapshots sandboxes. Joint KV+sandbox budgeting: none found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Keep cheap raw tokens on flash and let attention mass on a gist trigger exact re-prefill. Lossy KV compression becomes a recoverable cache with fidelity on demand.
killer_doubt: Re-prefilling a 4k-token chunk on a 70B model is ~0.57 PFLOP, about a 1 s stall. Above one zoom per ~50 tokens, throughput collapses. Chunk-local re-prefill loses cross-chunk context.
decisive_experiment: Llama-3.1-8B with Activation-Beacon-style 16-32x gists on RULER, LongBench-v2 and agent traces. Log gist-attention triggers and compare accuracy recovered with zoom on and off against the zoom rate. Under $50k of GPU time.
prior_art: Gist tokens (Mu et al. 2023), Activation Beacon, ICAE, InfLLM block retrieval, CacheBlend selective recompute. The attention-triggered re-prefill from raw tokens is the new twist.

key_insight: Compute can substitute for memory: token IDs are about 10^5 times smaller than KV. This is already the default eviction policy of every prefix cache.
killer_doubt: Regrowing a 32k-token context on a 70B model costs ~4.5 PFLOP (5-9 GPU-seconds). Inference GPUs are rarely idle, so flash-stored KV usually beats recompute on cost.
decisive_experiment: None needed. Reproduce Cake/InferCept results on a trace to confirm the recompute-vs-load crossover (tokens per GB/s of flash), then fold the result into I-08555's tier policy.
prior_art: InferCept (ICML 2024) chooses discard, swap or preserve; Cake (2024) computes and loads at once; HCache restores from hidden states; vLLM/SGLang evict and recompute.

key_insight: Bits per KV element can track token importance over time. This is a valid principle, but crowded.
killer_doubt: The baseline already ships FP8/NVFP4 KV (~4.5 bits including scales). Going to a ~3-bit average adds only ~1.4x, not 5x, and INT2 erodes multi-hop retrieval.
decisive_experiment: None decisive at <$1M beyond published work. A KIVI/ZipCache ablation over an NVFP4 baseline would only confirm an incremental ~1.3-1.5x.
prior_art: KIVI (2-bit, FP16 recent window), SKVQ sliding window, MiKV, ZipCache saliency, KVQuant, GEAR; NVFP4 KV cache deployed on Blackwell.

key_insight: In-batch duplicate of I-04883: age-graded KV precision decay on unchanged HBM.
killer_doubt: The incremental gain over shipped 4-bit FP KV is ~1.3-1.5x. Requantizing from 8 to 4 to 2 bits accumulates error on tokens later proven salient, and they cannot be re-sharpened.
decisive_experiment: None needed. This is covered by existing KIVI/SKVQ/ZipCache results.
prior_art: Same as I-04883: KIVI, SKVQ, MiKV, ZipCache, PM-KVQ; NVFP4 KV in production.

key_insight: Bounding attention scores from page summaries cuts KV traffic about 10-30x, but that mechanism is Quest, published almost verbatim.
killer_doubt: Exact prior art. Also, with the tail on NAND, ~80 us reads times 80 layer-serial lookups add ~6 ms per token, about 25% of a decode step.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. To keep a sliver of value, measure Quest+ArkVale with a NAND-resident tail on a single GPU to quantify the latency penalty. About $20k.
prior_art: Quest (ICML 2024) keeps per-page min/max key bounds; ArkVale, ShadowKV, InfiniGen, MagicPIG, RetroInfer offload the tail to CPU/SSD.

key_insight: Constant-size recurrent state does remove the growing KV term. Frontier labs already ship such hybrids, so a $1M team adds nothing.
killer_doubt: Not SRAM-sized. Mamba-2 state is ~2 MB per layer (8192x128 at FP16), ~100 MB per sequence. Batch 256 needs ~25 GB, far beyond ~50 MB of L2.
decisive_experiment: None in scope. Training a competitive hybrid needs well over $1M of compute. Distilling a small model only replicates published Jamba/Samba results.
prior_art: Jamba, Samba, Zamba, NVIDIA Nemotron-H, Qwen3-Next (Gated DeltaNet), MiniMax lightning attention, Kimi Linear.

key_insight: Installed SRAM capacity could stand in for DRAM in tiny-working-set services. The underlying problem is real: stranded DRAM.
killer_doubt: Genoa-X's 1.1 GB L3 is twelve private 96 MB CCD slices, so 1 GB working sets are not resident. Small services are already bin-packed: stranded DRAM is ~25%, not 80-95%.
decisive_experiment: Pin a 1 GB-working-set Redis or rate-limiter on a 9684X with one DIMM per channel. Measure DRAM bandwidth and p99 against a standard host. About $15k. A null result is expected.
prior_art: AMD 3D V-Cache (Milan-X/Genoa-X); Microsoft Pond and CXL pooling for stranded memory; standard Kubernetes bin-packing.

key_insight: Depth-first tile fusion with halo recompute removes intermediate DRAM traffic in conv stacks. This is valid and well known.
killer_doubt: DiT and video models use global self-attention, so after one attention layer the halo becomes the whole image. The 10-50x claim holds only for conv or local-window stacks.
decisive_experiment: None decisive. Compiler-fusion results already exist. Profiling a DiT step would confirm that attention blocks force full feature-map materialization.
prior_art: Fused-layer CNN accelerators (Alwani, MICRO 2016), MCUNetV2 patch inference (2021), DeFiNES (2023), TVM/XLA fusion, FlashAttention-style tiling.
